trace.situation: UK MARPOL implementing regulations cover investigation of reported oil traces near a ship, prohibition of hazardous chemical discharges, retention of oil residues, special area status timing for the Red Sea/Gulf of Aden/Oman area, and prohibition of certain substances in the Antarctic Area.
trace.trigger: Report received of visible oil traces on or below the sea surface in the vicinity of a ship or its wake; or a vessel operating in the Red Sea/Gulf of Aden/Oman area or the Antarctic Area.

procedures.action: On receipt of a report of visible oil traces near a ship, launch an investigation so far as reasonably practicable to determine if the regulation has been contravened.
procedures.why: Required to establish whether a discharge violation occurred.

procedures.action: Examine wind and sea conditions, the ship's track and speed, other possible sources of the oil traces, and relevant oil discharge records during the investigation.
procedures.why: These factors are specified as necessary elements of a proper investigation under paragraph (5).

procedures.action: Do not discharge chemicals/substances hazardous to the marine environment, or any substance intended to circumvent discharge conditions.
procedures.why: Such discharges are prohibited outright under the regulation.

procedures.action: Retain on board any oil residues that cannot be discharged in compliance with regulation 34 of Annex I, for later discharge to reception facilities.
procedures.why: Prevents non-compliant discharge into the sea.

procedures.action: Until the IMO publishes/establishes special area status for the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden, or Oman area, comply with regulations 25 and 26 discharge requirements as if the area were not a special area.
procedures.why: Special area status is only effective from the date IMO establishes it and publishes notice; until then normal (non-special-area) discharge rules apply.

procedures.action: Do not carry in bulk as cargo, use as ballast, or carry/use as fuel any substance listed in regulation 43.1 of Annex I while in the Antarctic Area, unless engaged in ship safety or search and rescue operations.
procedures.why: These substances are prohibited in the Antarctic Area to protect that environment, with an exception for safety/SAR vessels.

procedures.action: Do not require tank or pipeline cleaning/flushing after prior carriage/use of the prohibited Antarctic substances.
procedures.why: Regulation explicitly states such cleaning/flushing is not required in this circumstance.

constraints: Investigation obligation is qualified by 'so far as is reasonably practicable'.
Special area status for Red Sea/Gulf of Aden/Oman only applies once IMO establishes it and publishes notice on its website.
Antarctic Area substance prohibition does not apply to vessels engaged in ensuring ship safety or search and rescue.
Oil residues not compliant with regulation 34 of Annex I must be retained on board, not discharged.
warnings: Discharge of chemicals/substances hazardous to the marine environment is prohibited.
Discharge of substances intended to circumvent discharge conditions is prohibited.
Carriage/use of listed substances in the Antarctic Area as cargo, ballast, or fuel is prohibited except for safety/SAR vessels.
outcomes: An investigation determines whether the discharge regulation has been contravened based on conditions, track/speed, other sources, and discharge records.
Ships in the Red Sea/Gulf of Aden/Oman area continue under standard (non-special-area) discharge rules until IMO formally notifies special area status.
Oil residues retained on board are discharged later into shore reception facilities instead of the sea.
key_facts: The Secretary of State must investigate reports of visible oil traces near a ship so far as reasonably practicable.
Investigations must examine wind/sea conditions, ship track/speed, other oil sources, and discharge records.
Hazardous chemical discharges and discharges meant to circumvent rules are prohibited outright.
Red Sea, Gulf of Aden, and Oman area special area status takes effect only once the IMO establishes and publishes notice.
In the Antarctic Area, carriage/use of certain Annex I-listed substances is banned except for safety/SAR vessels, and tank cleaning after such use is not required.

trace.trigger: A ship intends to discharge sewage into the sea, either during normal operations, in a special area, in polar waters, or following an emergency/damage situation.

procedures.action: If outside a special area, discharge sewage only in accordance with Part A of regulation 11 (applies to non-passenger ships everywhere and passenger ships outside special areas).
procedures.why: Part A sets the standard conditions for lawful discharge outside special areas.

procedures.action: If a passenger ship operating in a special area from the relevant IMO-determined date, discharge only per Part B of regulation 11.
procedures.why: Passenger ships in special areas are subject to stricter requirements once the relevant date applies.

procedures.action: If a UK ship in polar waters, discharge sewage only in accordance with chapter 4, part II-A of the Polar Code.
procedures.why: Polar waters have additional pollution-prevention requirements beyond standard Annex IV rules.

procedures.action: Assess whether an exception applies: necessity for safety of ship/persons, saving life at sea, accidental discharge from damage (with reasonable precautions taken), or discharge under a foreign State's less stringent jurisdictional requirements.
procedures.why: These are the only recognised exceptions permitting discharge outside the normal regulated framework.

procedures.action: If sewage is mixed with waste/waste water covered by another MARPOL Annex, apply this regulation in addition to the other Annex's requirements.
procedures.why: Mixed waste streams must satisfy all applicable Annex requirements concurrently, not just one.

constraints: Discharge of sewage into the sea is prohibited unless one of the listed exceptions or regulation 11 provisions applies.

trace.trigger: A ship intends to proceed to sea from a port in the United Kingdom without a valid Sewage Certificate or without current survey documentation.

procedures.action: Confirm a valid Sewage Certificate has been issued under Annex IV before a Contracting State ship departs a UK port.
procedures.why: Departure without a valid certificate is prohibited unless alternative conditions are met.

procedures.action: If no valid certificate exists, obtain surveyor confirmation that the ship can proceed without presenting an unreasonable threat of harm to the marine environment.
procedures.why: This is an alternative lawful basis for departure in absence of a valid certificate.

procedures.action: If neither certificate nor surveyor satisfaction applies, obtain permission from a person with detention powers to proceed to the nearest appropriate repair yard.

trace.situation: UK regulations governing when a Certifying Authority or surveyor may extend or endorse the validity period of a ship's Sewage Certificate under MARPOL Annex IV implementation rules.

Does not apply to seafarers on fishing vessels.

Does not apply to seafarers on wooden ships of primitive build.
outcomes: A seafarer on an excluded vessel type is not subject to the requirements of this Part of the regulations.
key_facts: The Part applies to seafarers on UK-registered seagoing ships, unless excluded.

trace.situation: UK STCW regulations establish that seafarers must hold appropriate certificates of competency (or equivalent/third-party recognised certificates) matching their category, capacity and level of responsibility in order to be qualified to serve on board under manning requirements.

procedures.action: Verify each seafarer holds an appropriate certificate of competency or certificate of equivalent competency matching their listed category and capacity in Schedule 2.
procedures.why: A seafarer must meet the standards of competence specified to be qualified for manning purposes under section 47 of the Act.

procedures.action: Confirm the certificate is issued and endorsed in accordance with Part requirements and matches the ship's type, GT/power, propulsion, and the particular voyage.
procedures.why: The certificate only entitles the holder to act within the specific capacity, level of responsibility, ship type and voyage indicated by its endorsement.

procedures.action: Where a seafarer lacks an appropriate certificate, check whether they hold a valid third-party State certificate and have applied under regulation 37 or 38 for recognition.
procedures.why: The Secretary of State may permit such a seafarer to act in the capacity for a maximum of three months only under these specified circumstances.

procedures.action: Consider issuance or acceptance of an alternative certificate if consistent with STCW Regulation VII.
procedures.why: An alternative certification route is permitted when required under this regulation and in accordance with STCW Regulation VII.

constraints: Certificate must correspond to the exact category/capacity listed in column 1 of the Schedule 2 Table.
Certificate validity is limited to the specified ship type, GT/power, propulsion means, and particular voyage.
Temporary permission for a seafarer without an appropriate certificate is capped at three months.
Temporary permission requires a valid third-party State certificate and a pending application under regulation 37 or 38.
warnings: A certificate does not entitle the holder to act outside the specified capacity, level of responsibility, ship type/GT/power/propulsion, or voyage indicated.
outcomes: A seafarer without a compliant certificate (or valid temporary permission) is not qualified for manning purposes under section 47.
Temporary permission lapses after three months if full recognition is not granted.
key_facts: Certificates of competency or equivalent competency must align with Schedule 2 category and capacity criteria.
A certificate's validity is scoped to level of responsibility, ship type/GT/power/propulsion, and the particular voyage.
Temporary service without an appropriate certificate is allowed for up to three months under specific third-party certificate conditions.
Alternative certification is possible under STCW Regulation VII.

trace.situation: UK STCW regulations specify certification requirements for seafarers assigned to cargo operations on oil tankers and chemical tankers.
trace.trigger: A seafarer is to serve as master, chief engineer officer, chief mate, second engineer officer, or any crew member with immediate responsibility for loading, discharging, cargo care in transit, tank cleaning, or other cargo-related operations aboard an oil tanker or chemical tanker.

procedures.action: Confirm that the master, chief engineer officer, chief mate, second engineer officer, and any seafarer with cargo-operation responsibilities hold a certificate of proficiency in advanced training for the relevant tanker type (oil or chemical).
procedures.why: Regulation applies these certification requirements specifically to these roles due to their direct involvement in cargo operations.

procedures.action: Obtain the certificate of proficiency from the Secretary of State (for those meeting STCW V/1-1 para 4 or 6 criteria) or from an approved training provider (for non-master/officer personnel meeting the same criteria).
procedures.why: The regulation designates two valid issuing authorities depending on the seafarer's rank and qualification pathway.

procedures.action: For masters and officers, verify that the certificate of competency has been endorsed by the Secretary of State under regulation 34 as an alternative means of satisfying the certificate of proficiency requirement.
procedures.why: Endorsement under regulation 34 is deemed to satisfy the advanced training certification requirement for masters/officers.

constraints: Only applies to seafarers on oil tankers or chemical tankers in the specified roles.
Certificate of proficiency must be issued either by the Secretary of State or an approved training provider, depending on rank.
Masters/officers must meet the requirement via certificate of competency endorsement under regulation 34, not via an approved training provider.
channels: Regulation 34 (endorsements on a certificate of competency)
outcomes: Seafarers without the required certificate of proficiency (or equivalent endorsement) are not qualified to perform cargo operations on oil or chemical tankers under this regulation.
Proper endorsement under regulation 34 allows masters/officers to satisfy the advanced training certification requirement without a separate certificate of proficiency.
key_facts: The regulation covers master, chief engineer officer, chief mate, second engineer officer, and any seafarer with immediate cargo-operation responsibility.
Oil tanker cargo operations require advanced training certification per STCW V/1-1 paragraph 4; chemical tanker operations require certification per STCW V/1-1 paragraph 6.
Certificates of proficiency can be issued by the Secretary of State or an approved training provider, with approved training providers limited to non-master/officer personnel.
A certificate of competency endorsed under regulation 34 satisfies the certificate of proficiency requirement for masters and officers.

trace.situation: UK STCW regulations specify certification requirements for three categories of seafarers: engine room watchkeepers on vessels with 350-750kW propulsion power, GMDSS radio operators, and personnel handling cargo/cargo equipment on oil or chemical tankers.
trace.trigger: A seafarer is assigned to engine room watchkeeping duties, GMDSS radio duties, or oil/chemical tanker cargo operations duties.

procedures.action: Verify engine room watchkeepers on ships with propulsion power 350-749kW hold either an engineering certificate of competency (reg. 7) or an approved marine engine operator's licence per specified MSN criteria.
procedures.why: Regulation requires one of these qualifications before the seafarer may perform watchkeeping duties in that power range.

procedures.action: Confirm GMDSS radio duty holders are at least 18 years old and have completed training meeting STCW Code section A-IV/2 standards before issuing a certificate of competency.
procedures.why: The Secretary of State may not issue a GMDSS certificate unless these age and competence criteria are met.

procedures.action: Ensure personnel assigned cargo or cargo equipment duties on oil/chemical tankers hold a certificate of proficiency in basic training for tanker cargo operations, issued either by the Secretary of State or an approved training provider per STCW Regulation V/1-1 paragraph 2.
procedures.why: Mandatory minimum requirements for basic training on oil and chemical tankers must be satisfied before assignment.

procedures.action: For masters/officers on tankers, confirm the certificate of competency has been endorsed under regulation 34 in lieu of a separate certificate of proficiency.
procedures.why: Endorsement under regulation 34 satisfies the certificate of proficiency requirement for masters and officers.

constraints: Engine room watchkeeping rule applies only to ships with propulsion power at least 350kW but less than 750kW.
GMDSS certificate of competency cannot be issued to anyone under 18 years of age.
GMDSS certificate requires meeting STCW Code section A-IV/2 standards.
Oil/chemical tanker cargo certificate of proficiency issuance differs depending on whether the person is a master/officer or other crew.
warnings: A certificate of competency for GMDSS duties may not be issued unless age and training criteria are fully met.
Cargo/cargo equipment duties on oil or chemical tankers must not be assigned without the required certificate of proficiency.
outcomes: Properly certificated engine room watchkeepers, GMDSS operators, and tanker cargo personnel ensure compliance with STCW mandatory minimum standards.
Failure to hold the required certificates would make assignment of these duties non-compliant with UK STCW regulations.
key_facts: The engine room watchkeeping certification rule applies specifically to ships with propulsion power between 350kW and 750kW.
GMDSS certificate holders must be at least 18 years old and trained to STCW Code A-IV/2 standards.
Oil/chemical tanker cargo duty personnel need a certificate of proficiency in basic training, issued by the Secretary of State or an approved training provider depending on rank.
Masters and officers can satisfy the tanker cargo proficiency requirement via endorsement of their certificate of competency under regulation 34.

trace.situation: STCW regulation sets certification requirements for seafarers assigned cargo-related duties and responsibilities aboard liquefied gas tankers.
trace.trigger: A seafarer is assigned specific duties or responsibilities related to cargo or cargo equipment on a liquefied gas tanker.

procedures.action: Confirm that any officer or rating assigned cargo-related duties on a liquefied gas tanker holds a certificate of proficiency in basic training for liquefied gas tanker cargo operations.
procedures.why: Required under paragraph (1) before assignment to such duties.

procedures.action: For master, chief engineer officer, chief mate, second engineer officer, or any seafarer with immediate responsibility for loading, discharging, care in transit, handling of cargo, or tank cleaning, confirm an advanced training certificate of proficiency is held.
procedures.why: Paragraph (2) imposes a higher advanced training standard on these specified senior/responsible roles.

procedures.action: Verify the certificate was issued either by the Secretary of State (for persons meeting STCW V/1-2 para 2 or para 4 criteria) or by an approved training provider (for non-master/officer personnel).
procedures.why: Specifies the only valid issuing authorities for basic and advanced certificates.

procedures.action: For a master or officer, confirm the Secretary of State has endorsed their certificate of competency under regulation 34 in lieu of a separate proficiency certificate.
procedures.why: Endorsement under regulation 34 satisfies the certificate of proficiency requirement for masters and officers.

constraints: Only seafarers assigned specific cargo or cargo-equipment duties on a liquefied gas tanker fall under paragraph (1).
Regulation (advanced training) applies specifically to master, chief engineer officer, chief mate, second engineer officer, and any seafarer with immediate cargo operation responsibility.
Certificates must meet STCW Regulation V/1-2 paragraph 2 (basic) or paragraph 4 (advanced) criteria.
For masters/officers, certificate requirement is only satisfied via Secretary of State endorsement under regulation 34, not via approved training provider issuance.
outcomes: Personnel without the required basic or advanced certificate of proficiency are not qualified to be assigned the corresponding cargo-related duties on a liquefied gas tanker.

Advanced training certification applies specifically to master, chief engineer officer, chief mate, second engineer officer, and any seafarer with immediate cargo operation responsibility.

Master/officer certificate requirements are satisfied via Secretary of State endorsement under regulation 34.

trace.situation: UK STCW regulations specify certification requirements for ratings serving as navigational watch members, engine-room watch members, able seafarers deck, and able seafarers engine on qualifying vessels.
trace.trigger: A rating is assigned to form part of a navigational or engine-room watch, or to serve as able seafarer deck/engine, on a ship meeting the specified gross tonnage or propulsion power thresholds.

procedures.action: Verify that any rating forming part of a navigational watch on a ship of 500 GT or more holds a valid certificate of proficiency.
procedures.why: Regulation requires such certification unless the rating is under training or performs unskilled duties.

procedures.action: Verify that any rating forming part of an engine-room watch, or designated for periodically unmanned engine-room duty, on a ship with main propulsion of 750 kW or more holds a valid certificate of proficiency.
procedures.why: Same mandatory minimum requirement scheme applies to engine-room watch ratings under STCW Regulation III/4.

procedures.action: Confirm able seafarer deck personnel on ships of 500 GT or more hold the required certificate of proficiency per STCW II/5.
procedures.why: Certification ensures minimum competency standards for able seafarer deck role.

procedures.action: Confirm able seafarer engine personnel on ships with propulsion of 750 kW or more hold the required certificate of proficiency per STCW III/5.
procedures.why: Certification ensures minimum competency standards for able seafarer engine role.

constraints: Applies only to ships of 500 GT or more (navigational watch, able seafarer deck) or 750 kW or more propulsion power (engine-room watch, able seafarer engine).
Certificates may only be issued by the Secretary of State or an approved training provider to persons meeting the specified STCW criteria.
The navigational and engine-room watch certification requirement does not apply to ratings under training or those performing unskilled duties.
warnings: A rating without the required certificate of proficiency must not be assigned to navigational or engine-room watch duties, or serve as able seafarer deck/engine, on a qualifying vessel.
outcomes: Properly certificated ratings ensure the ship meets mandatory minimum STCW competency standards for watchkeeping and able seafarer roles.
key_facts: Navigational watch rating certification applies to ships of 500 GT or more.
Engine-room watch rating certification applies to ships with propulsion power of 750 kW or more.
Exemptions exist for ratings under training or with unskilled duties, but only for watch-rating certificates, not able seafarer certificates.
Able seafarer deck and able seafarer engine certificates follow separate STCW provisions (II/5 and III/5 respectively).

trace.situation: Statutory requirements for certification of seafarers' basic and advanced training for service on ships subject to the IGF Code (gas/low-flashpoint fuel ships).
trace.trigger: A seafarer is assigned designated safety duties or responsibility for care, use of, or emergency response to fuel on board a ship subject to the IGF Code.

procedures.action: Confirm that any seafarer with designated safety duties related to fuel on an IGF Code ship holds a certificate of proficiency in basic training for IGF Code service.
procedures.why: Regulation requires this certificate for such personnel per paragraph (2).

procedures.action: Verify the certificate was issued by the Secretary of State or an approved training provider to a person meeting STCW Regulation V/3 paragraph 5 criteria.
procedures.why: Only persons meeting these mandatory minimum requirements may be issued the certificate.

procedures.action: Accept equivalent certification (regulation 13(2) or 14(3) liquefied gas tanker cargo training) as satisfying basic IGF Code training requirements where applicable.
procedures.why: These certificates are deemed to meet the basic training requirement under paragraph (3).

procedures.action: Confirm that the master, engineer officers, and any seafarer with immediate responsibility for fuel/fuel systems on an IGF Code ship hold advanced training certification.
procedures.why: These specific roles are designated as requiring advanced training under the regulation.

procedures.action: Verify advanced certificates were issued to persons meeting STCW Regulation V/3 paragraph 8 criteria, or accept basic liquefied gas tanker certification plus compliance with paragraph 9 alternative criteria as equivalent.
procedures.why: These are the recognized pathways to meeting advanced training requirements.

constraints: Certificate of basic training is required for any seafarer with designated safety duties relating to fuel on IGF Code ships.
Certificate of advanced training is required specifically for the master, engineer officers, and seafarers with immediate responsibility for fuel/fuel systems.
Certificates may only be issued by the Secretary of State or an approved training provider.
Issuance is conditioned on meeting specific STCW Regulation V/3 criteria (paragraph 5 for basic, paragraph 8 for advanced, or paragraph 9 as alternative).
outcomes: Seafarers without the required certificate of proficiency cannot be assigned fuel-related safety duties on IGF Code ships.
Equivalent liquefied gas tanker cargo training certificates can substitute for IGF Code basic/advanced training certification where criteria are met.
key_facts: Two tiers of IGF Code fuel training certification exist: basic (for designated safety duty personnel) and advanced (for master, engineer officers, and those with immediate fuel system responsibility).
Certificates can only be issued by the Secretary of State or an approved training provider.
Certification criteria are defined by STCW Regulation V/3 paragraphs 5 (basic), 8 (advanced), and 9 (alternative advanced criteria).
Liquefied gas tanker cargo operation certificates (basic or advanced) can be recognized as equivalent to IGF Code training certificates under specified conditions.

trace.situation: UK STCW implementing regulations setting out certification requirements for electro-technical ratings, survival craft/rescue boat operators, fast rescue boat operators, and ship security officers.
trace.trigger: A seafarer is to be assigned duties as an electro-technical rating, survival craft/rescue boat operator, fast rescue boat operator, or ship security officer aboard a qualifying vessel.

procedures.action: Confirm electro-technical ratings on ships with main propulsion machinery of 750 kW or more hold a valid certificate of proficiency.
procedures.why: Mandatory requirement under STCW Regulation III/7, paragraph 2 or 4.

procedures.action: Confirm any seafarer designated to launch or take charge of a survival craft or rescue boat (non-fast) holds the relevant certificate of proficiency.
procedures.why: Required by STCW Regulation VI/2, paragraph 1.

procedures.action: Confirm any seafarer designated to launch or take charge of a fast rescue boat holds the relevant certificate of proficiency.
procedures.why: Required by STCW Regulation VI/2, paragraph 2.

procedures.action: Confirm the ship security officer holds a certificate of proficiency for that role before assigning security duties.
procedures.why: Required by STCW Regulation VI/5, paragraph 1.

procedures.action: Ensure only the Secretary of State or an approved training provider issues these certificates, and only to persons meeting the specified STCW criteria.
procedures.why: Certificates may only be issued to persons meeting the mandatory minimum requirements in the cited STCW regulations.

constraints: Applies to ships with main propulsion machinery of 750 kW or more for electro-technical ratings.

warnings: A seafarer without the required certificate of proficiency must not be designated to launch/take charge of survival craft, rescue boats, fast rescue boats, or act as ship security officer, or serve as an electro-technical rating on qualifying ships.
outcomes: Compliance ensures only properly certificated seafarers perform safety-critical and security functions aboard ship.

Separate certificates of proficiency are required for survival craft/rescue boats versus fast rescue boats.
Ship security officers must hold a specific certificate of proficiency per STCW Regulation VI/5.

trace.situation: STCW regulation sets out mandatory training requirements for seafarers assigned to duties on board passenger ships (other than high speed craft) engaged on international voyages.
trace.trigger: A seafarer is to be assigned shipboard duties on a passenger ship engaged on international voyages.

procedures.action: Ensure the seafarer completes required training per their capacity, duties and responsibilities before being assigned shipboard duties on a passenger ship.
procedures.why: Regulation mandates training completion prior to assignment of duties.

procedures.action: Ensure master, each officer, and seafarers designated on muster lists to assist passengers complete crowd management training (STCW Code A-V/2 para 3).
procedures.why: These personnel are responsible for managing passengers during emergencies.

procedures.action: Ensure seafarers providing direct service to passengers in passenger spaces complete safety training (STCW Code A-V/2 para 2).
procedures.why: Required for personnel in direct contact with passengers.

procedures.action: Ensure master, chief engineer officer, chief mate, second engineer officer, and seafarers responsible for embarking/disembarking passengers, cargo operations, or hull opening closures on ro-ro passenger ships complete passenger safety, cargo safety and hull integrity training (STCW Code A-V/2 para 5).
procedures.why: These roles carry immediate responsibility for operations affecting passenger and vessel safety.

procedures.action: Ensure master, chief engineer officer, chief mate, second engineer officer, and seafarers designated with responsibility for passenger safety in emergencies complete crisis management and human behaviour training (STCW Code A-V/2 para 4).
procedures.why: These senior roles must manage crisis situations and human behaviour during emergencies.

procedures.action: Ensure all seafarers on board complete passenger ship emergency familiarisation training appropriate to their role (STCW Code A-V/2 para 1).
procedures.why: General emergency familiarisation is required for all seafarers regardless of specific duties.

constraints: Applies only to passenger ships engaged on international voyages, excluding high speed craft.
Training must be completed prior to assignment of shipboard duties.
Specific training requirements depend on the seafarer's capacity, duties and responsibilities.
outcomes: Properly trained crew are able to manage crowds, provide direct passenger service, handle cargo/hull integrity operations, and manage crisis situations effectively.
Non-compliance would leave seafarers unprepared for passenger ship emergency duties, risking passenger safety.
key_facts: The regulation applies to seafarers on passenger ships engaged on international voyages, excluding high speed craft.
Crowd management training is required for the master, officers, and muster-list-designated passenger assistance personnel.
Safety training is required for seafarers providing direct service to passengers in passenger spaces.
Passenger safety, cargo safety and hull integrity training is required for master, chief engineer officer, chief mate, second engineer officer, and relevant ro-ro cargo/hull personnel.
Crisis management and human behaviour training is required for master, chief engineer officer, chief mate, second engineer officer, and muster-list-designated emergency responsibility seafarers.

trace.situation: UK STCW regulations specify mandatory certification and training requirements for seafarers before assignment to shipboard duties, covering high speed craft type rating, basic safety familiarisation, and advanced fire fighting.
trace.trigger: A seafarer is about to be assigned shipboard duties on a high speed craft, or any vessel, or is designated to control fire-fighting operations.

procedures.action: Before assigning a seafarer to duties on a high speed craft built on/after 1 Jan 1996, ensure completion of type rating training per HSC Code para 18.3.3.
procedures.why: Regulation requires completion before shipboard duties are assigned.

procedures.action: Obtain documentary evidence (certificate per MSN 1740(M) for masters/officers) from Secretary of State or approved training provider upon successful completion.
procedures.why: Certification confirms competence and is legally required evidence.

procedures.action: Before assigning any seafarer to shipboard duties, ensure they have received safety familiarisation and basic training per STCW Code section A-VI/1 and hold a certificate of proficiency.
procedures.why: Mandatory minimum requirement for all seafarers to meet standard of competence.

procedures.action: Before designating a seafarer to control fire-fighting operations, ensure completion of advanced fire fighting training per STCW Code section A-VI/3 and issuance of corresponding certificate.
procedures.why: Mandatory minimum training requirement for personnel controlling fire-fighting operations.

constraints: Applies only to high speed craft constructed on or after 1 January 1996.
Certificates may only be issued to seafarers who meet both the training and competence standard requirements.

warnings: A seafarer must not be assigned shipboard duties on applicable high speed craft without completed type rating training.

Advanced fire fighting training follows STCW Code section A-VI/3 and is mandatory for those controlling fire-fighting operations.
Certificates can only be issued by the Secretary of State or an approved training provider.

trace.situation: STCW regulatory requirements specifying competence and certification standards for seafarers providing medical first aid/medical care and for seafarers requiring security-awareness or security-duty training under the ISPS Code.
trace.trigger: A seafarer is designated to provide medical first aid, take charge of medical care, or is assigned shipboard duties on a ship required to comply with the ISPS Code.

procedures.action: Ensure a seafarer designated for medical first aid meets STCW Code section A-VI/4 paragraphs 1-3 and holds a certificate of proficiency in medical first aid.

procedures.action: Ensure a seafarer designated to take charge of medical care meets STCW Code section A-VI/4 paragraphs 4-6 and holds a certificate of proficiency in medical care.

procedures.action: Confirm certificates of proficiency are issued only by the Secretary of State or an approved training provider to seafarers meeting the specified competence paragraphs.

procedures.action: Before assigning shipboard duties, ensure seafarer receives security-awareness familiarisation/training per STCW Code section A-VI/6 paragraphs 1-4 and holds a certificate of proficiency in security-awareness.
procedures.why: Mandatory under ISPS Code applicability for seagoing ships.

procedures.action: Ensure seafarers with designated security duties meet STCW Code section A-VI/6 paragraphs 6-8 and hold a certificate of competency in security duties.

outcomes: Properly certified seafarers ensure compliant medical and security coverage on board.

Seafarers with designated security duties need STCW A-VI/6 paragraphs 6-8 competence and a certificate of competency.

trace.situation: UK Merchant Shipping STCW regulations set out the administrative requirements for applying for, issuing, and endorsing certificates of competency and proficiency for seafarers.

procedures.action: Submit application for a certificate or licence in the form specified by the Secretary of State, with the prescribed fee and evidence of identity, age, relevant service, standards of competence and certificates/qualifications held.
procedures.why: Required content for a valid application under this Part.

procedures.action: Submit applications for ancillary matters (e.g. certified copies) in the specified form with the prescribed fee, plus evidence of issue by the approved training provider where applicable.
procedures.why: Ensures ancillary certificate requests are properly substantiated.

procedures.action: Issue certificates of competency/proficiency in the form specified in STCW Code section A-I/2, paragraph 1.

trace.situation: UK regulation governing how the Secretary of State may recognise certificates of competency, tanker cargo operations proficiency, and other proficiency certificates issued by EEA States party to the STCW Convention, and issue UK certificates of equivalent competency.

procedures.action: On request from an EEA State, third party State, or an employing/prospective employing company, Registrar provides relevant register information.
procedures.why: Necessary to verify the authenticity or validity of documents held by a seafarer.

procedures.action: A person wishing to provide seafarer training/assessment must apply for approval by the Secretary of State.
procedures.why: Ensures training providers meet required standards before certifying seafarers.

procedures.action: Demonstrate qualifications/experience under STCW Code Section A-I/6, meet relevant Merchant Shipping Notices, and pay the prescribed fee.

constraints: Application for certified copy must be in the Secretary of State's specified form.

Evidence of original issuance required for certificates of proficiency from approved training providers.
Register information disclosed only to the extent necessary to verify authenticity or validity of documents.
Training/assessment providers must be approved before providing certification-related training.
Approval requires compliance with STCW Code Section A-I/6 and relevant Merchant Shipping Notices, plus fee payment.
outcomes: A certified copy of a lost/deprived certificate may be issued once requirements are met.
Verification information from the register supports confirming authenticity of seafarer documents to requesting states/companies.
A person failing to meet qualification, notice compliance, or fee requirements will not be approved as a training/assessment provider.

The Registrar keeps a register of certificates and endorsements for verification purposes.

trace.situation: UK STCW regulations set out the grounds for suspension or cancellation of seafarer certificates, and the notice and inquiry procedures that apply when a certificate is refused, suspended, or cancelled.
trace.trigger: The holder is convicted of an offence under section 47(5) of the Act (false statement etc.), or conditions for issue/endorsement of a certificate have not been complied with, or the Secretary of State/approved training provider intends to refuse, suspend, revalidate-refuse, or cancel a certificate.

procedures.action: Suspend or cancel a certificate where the holder is convicted under section 47(5) or conditions for issue/endorsement were not met.
procedures.why: Maintains integrity of certification system against false statements or non-compliance.

procedures.action: Give written notice to the applicant/holder before refusing, revalidating-refusing, suspending, or cancelling a certificate.
procedures.why: Ensures due process and informs the party of the adverse decision.

procedures.action: Require approved training providers to give written notice when refusing to issue/revalidate a certificate of proficiency or refusing documentary evidence under regulations 26 or 49(2).
procedures.why: Extends the same procedural fairness to decisions delegated to training providers.

procedures.action: Accept electronic notice as satisfying the 'in writing' requirement if it is transmitted electronically, received legibly, and retrievable for later reference.
procedures.why: Allows modern communication methods while preserving evidentiary reliability.

procedures.action: Allow the applicant to request, before a specified date, that the refusal/suspension/cancellation be reviewed at an inquiry.
procedures.why: Provides a right of appeal against adverse certificate decisions.

procedures.action: Treat a failure by the Secretary of State to issue/revalidate or give notice within 28 days of application as a deemed refusal, giving the applicant a further 28 days to demand an inquiry in writing.
procedures.why: Prevents indefinite delay from denying the applicant a remedy.

procedures.action: Hold an inquiry by one or more appointed persons when an applicant has required a review under paragraph (4) or (5).
procedures.why: Provides an independent review mechanism for contested decisions.

constraints: Notice of refusal/suspension/cancellation must be in writing (including qualifying electronic form).
Review must be requested before the date specified in the notice, or within 28 days after a deemed refusal.
Inquiry must be conducted by person(s) appointed by the Secretary of State.
warnings: Conviction for false statement under section 47(5) can result in certificate suspension or cancellation.
Failure to respond within 28 days results in deemed refusal of the application.
outcomes: Certificate holder may have certificate suspended or cancelled for misconduct or non-compliance.
Applicant can obtain an independent inquiry to review adverse certificate decisions.
Unresponsive applications are deemed refused after 28 days, preserving the applicant's right to further review.
key_facts: Certificates may be suspended/cancelled for false statement convictions or failure to meet issue/endorsement conditions.
Written notice (including qualifying electronic notice) is mandatory before refusal, suspension, or cancellation.
Approved training providers must also give written notice for refusals of proficiency certificates or documentary evidence.
Applicants can request a review inquiry before a specified date.
No action/notice within 28 days equals a deemed refusal, with a further 28-day window to demand inquiry.

trace.situation: UK STCW regulations set out the Secretary of State's process for approving, extending, altering, suspending or cancelling the approval of maritime training providers.
trace.trigger: A training provider applies for approval, seeks extension, or the Secretary of State reviews ongoing compliance of an approved provider.

procedures.action: Grant approval under paragraph (2) for a maximum of five years from the date in the approval letter.
procedures.why: Approvals are time-limited to ensure periodic review of training providers.

procedures.action: Extend approval in increments of up to five years only if the provider still meets paragraph (2)(a)-(b) requirements and has paid the prescribed fee.
procedures.why: Ensures continued compliance and administrative cost recovery before extension.

procedures.action: Alter, suspend or cancel an approval or extension only after giving reasonable notice.
procedures.why: Provides fairness and due process to the training provider.

procedures.action: Issue all approvals, extensions, alterations, suspensions or cancellations in writing, specifying effective date and terms.
procedures.why: Ensures clarity and legal certainty of the decision.

procedures.action: Accept electronic transmission as satisfying the 'in writing' requirement if received legibly and retrievable for future reference.
procedures.why: Modernises communication while preserving evidentiary standard.

procedures.action: Give written notice to the applicant if intending to refuse approval or an extension.
procedures.why: Ensures procedural fairness before an adverse decision.

procedures.action: Require the approved provider to continue complying with paragraph (2)(a)-(b) requirements throughout the approval's validity.
procedures.why: Maintains ongoing quality assurance, not just at time of approval.

procedures.action: Require surrender of the approval letter or certificate if directed by the Secretary of State.
procedures.why: Allows withdrawal of documentary evidence of approval when no longer valid.

procedures.action: Monitor and periodically evaluate approved training providers per STCW Regulation I/8 and relevant Merchant Shipping Notices.
procedures.why: Ensures sustained quality standards consistent with international STCW requirements.

constraints: Approval duration cannot exceed five years per grant or extension.
Extensions require continued compliance with paragraph (2)(a)-(b) and payment of the prescribed fee.
Any alteration, suspension or cancellation requires reasonable notice.
All formal decisions must be in writing, including electronic form meeting legibility and retrievability criteria.
Refusal decisions require written notice to the applicant.
warnings: Failure to continue meeting paragraph (2)(a)-(b) requirements may result in alteration, suspension, or cancellation of approval.
Non-payment of prescribed fee can block extension of approval.
outcomes: Compliant training providers retain or extend their approval status.
Non-compliant or non-paying providers risk refusal, suspension, or cancellation of approval.
Providers must surrender approval documents if directed, removing their authority to operate as approved.
key_facts: Approvals and extensions are capped at five years each.
Extensions require ongoing compliance with original approval criteria and fee payment.
Electronic communication can satisfy 'in writing' requirements if legible and retrievable.
The Secretary of State must give written notice before refusing approval or extension.
Approved providers are subject to ongoing monitoring under STCW Regulation I/8.

trace.situation: UK STCW regulation establishing an appeals/inquiry process for persons refused, or whose approval is altered, suspended or cancelled under, the training provider approval regime (regulation 48).
trace.trigger: A person is refused an approval (or extension) under regulation 48, or has an existing approval altered, suspended or cancelled under regulation 48(6).

procedures.action: Request the Secretary of State to hold an inquiry within 21 days of receiving notice of the decision and before the date specified in the notice.
procedures.why: This is the statutory time window within which an affected person may challenge the decision.

procedures.action: Secretary of State must cause an inquiry to be held by one or more appointed persons once validly requested.
procedures.why: Ensures due process and independent review of approval decisions affecting training providers.

constraints: Request for inquiry must be made within 21 days after receiving notice of the decision
Request must be made before the date specified in the notice
Only applies to decisions under regulation 48 (approval) or 48(6) (alteration, suspension or cancellation)
outcomes: If timely request made, Secretary of State must arrange an inquiry by appointed person(s)
If no timely request made, the decision presumably stands unchallenged
key_facts: Regulation 48 governs approval of training providers.
Regulation 48(6) governs alteration, suspension or cancellation of an approval.
Affected persons have 21 days from notice to request an inquiry, and must do so before the date specified in the notice.
Inquiries are held by one or more persons appointed by the Secretary of State.

trace.situation: UK STCW regulations establishing offences related to unauthorized provision of seafarer training/assessment and requirements for approved training providers to issue certificates or documentary evidence upon successful completion of training.
trace.trigger: A person or organisation offers, provides, advertises, or administers seafarer training/assessment for STCW certification, or a seafarer completes an approved training or assessment course.

procedures.action: Do not offer or provide training or assessment of seafarers for certification under this Part without a Secretary of State approval.
procedures.why: Unapproved provision of training/assessment is a prohibited offence under this regulation.

procedures.action: Do not use, lend, or allow another to use an approval with intent to deceive.
procedures.why: Prevents fraudulent misrepresentation of approval status.

procedures.action: Do not advertise or display an expired or unissued approval.
procedures.why: Protects integrity of the approval system and prevents misleading claims of authorisation.

procedures.action: Surrender approval letter or approval certificate when required under paragraph (11).
procedures.why: Ensures expired or revoked approvals are not retained or misused.

procedures.action: Issue a certificate of proficiency in the form specified in STCW Code Section A-I/2 to every person who successfully completes required training/assessment, except for master/officer tanker training under regulations 10-14.
procedures.why: Confirms compliance with STCW Code certification format requirements.

procedures.action: Issue documentary evidence (rather than a certificate) to masters/officers completing training under regulations 7-16, 25, or 43.
procedures.why: Differentiates certification requirements for specific categories of training (e.g., tanker, passenger ship, refresher training).

constraints: Only Secretary of State-approved providers may offer or provide STCW certification training/assessment.
Approval letters/certificates must be surrendered when required under paragraph (11).
Certificates of proficiency must follow the form specified in STCW Code Section A-I/2.
Master/officer tanker training under regulations 10-14 is excluded from the certificate-of-proficiency requirement.
Documentary evidence (not certificates) applies specifically to training under regulations 7-16, 25, and 43.
warnings: It is an offence to provide training/assessment for certification without approval.
It is an offence to use an approval with intent to deceive.
It is an offence to advertise or display an expired or unissued approval.
Failure to surrender a required approval letter or certificate is an offence.
outcomes: Unauthorized or fraudulent training provision exposes the provider to legal penalty under these regulations.
Successful completion of approved training results in issuance of a certificate of proficiency or documentary evidence, depending on the training category.

Fraudulent use or display of an approval is a specific offence.
Certificates of proficiency must conform to STCW Code Section A-I/2 format.

Approval letters and certificates must be surrendered when required under paragraph (11).

trace.situation: UK STCW regulation setting out master's and chief engineer's duties to ensure adequate watchkeeping arrangements at sea and in port.
trace.trigger: Ship is underway, moored, or at anchor and watchkeeping arrangements must be established and maintained.

procedures.action: Master ensures navigational, engineering and radio watchkeeping arrangements are adequate at all times.
procedures.why: Required under STCW Regulation VIII/2 paragraph 2 and section A-VIII/2 of the STCW Code, accounting for prevailing circumstances and conditions.

procedures.action: Master gives directions to deck watchkeeping officers for safe navigation during their duty periods.
procedures.why: Mandated by section A-VIII/2 Part 4-1 of the STCW Code and Merchant Shipping Notice 1868 (M) Amendment 1.

procedures.action: Chief engineer officer ensures engineering watchkeeping arrangements are adequate for a safe watch.
procedures.why: Required by section A-VIII/2 Part 4-2 of the STCW Code and MSN 1868 (M) Amendment 1.

procedures.action: Master arranges an appropriate and effective watch when ship is safely moored or anchored in port.
procedures.why: Required by section A-VIII/2 Part 5 of the STCW Code (watchkeeping in port) and MSN 1868 (M) Amendment 1, to ensure safety even when not underway.

constraints: Watchkeeping arrangements must be adequate at all times, not just during normal conditions.

procedures.action: Issue any exemption, alteration, or cancellation in writing.

procedures.action: Specify the effective date and any terms on which the exemption is given.
procedures.why: Required content ensures clarity on when and how the exemption applies.

procedures.action: Ensure electronic transmission of exemption documents is legible and retrievable for subsequent reference.

procedures.action: Comply with any safety requirements attached to an exemption under paragraph (2).
procedures.why: Failure to comply causes the exemption to automatically cease to have effect.

constraints: Exemption alterations/cancellations require reasonable notice.
Exemption granted under paragraph (2) ceases automatically if safety requirements are not met.

procedures.action: Company applying for a safe manning document must submit proposed numbers and grades of seafarers to the Secretary of State in the specified form.

procedures.action: Secretary of State issues the document only if proposals meet IMO Resolution A.1047(27) principles and the fee is paid.
procedures.why: Ensures manning proposals align with internationally recognized safe manning principles.

procedures.action: Company must notify the Secretary of State as soon as any pertinent circumstances change.

trace.situation: UK STCW regulations set out certification, training, and exemption requirements for seafarers serving on UK-registered seagoing hovercraft constructed on or after 1 January 1996.

procedures.action: Ensure every seafarer on board meets the specified standards of competence to be qualified under section 47 of the Act (manning).
procedures.why: Qualification for manning purposes depends on meeting these competence standards.

procedures.action: Owner must ensure the seafarer has completed training specified in paragraph 18.3.3 of the High Speed Craft Code (type rating training).
procedures.why: This training is mandated as part of the competence requirement under regulation 51.

procedures.action: Training provider must issue documentary evidence to each person who successfully completes the training.
procedures.why: Documentary evidence is required to prove completion of type rating training.

procedures.action: For masters/officers, issue a certificate in the form specified in Merchant Shipping Notice 1740(M), endorsed as specified.
procedures.why: The Secretary of State has prescribed a specific certificate form and endorsement method for masters/officers.

procedures.action: Apply regulations 31-34, 41, 42, 44, 45, and 46 to hovercraft certificates as they apply to Part 2 certificates.
procedures.why: These regulations govern application, issuing, validity, revalidation, suspension, cancellation, and appeal processes, extended to hovercraft certification for consistency.

procedures.action: Apply regulations 48-50 to training providers delivering type rating training under regulation 51(3).
procedures.why: Ensures training providers for hovercraft personnel are governed by the same oversight as Part 2 training providers.

procedures.action: Owner may apply to the Secretary of State for an exemption from regulation 51 requirements if compliance is impracticable or unreasonable.
procedures.why: The Secretary of State has discretion to grant exemptions for classes or individual cases where strict compliance is not feasible.

procedures.action: If an exemption is granted, comply with any additional safety requirements imposed by the Secretary of State.
procedures.why: Exemptions may be conditioned on safety requirements to preserve overall hovercraft safety.

constraints: Part applies only to UK-registered seagoing hovercraft constructed on or after 1 January 1996.
Seafarers must meet specified competence standards to be qualified under section 47 of the Act.
Master/officer certificates must use the form and endorsement specified in MSN 1740(M).
Exemptions may only be granted if compliance is impracticable or unreasonable, and may carry safety conditions.
warnings: A seafarer who has not completed the required training/competence standards is not qualified for manning purposes under section 47.
outcomes: Seafarers completing required training and holding properly endorsed certificates are qualified for manning under section 47.

procedures.action: If seeking relief from Part requirements, apply for exemption from the Secretary of State, who may grant it if compliance is impracticable or unreasonable.
procedures.why: Allows flexibility where strict compliance is not feasible, while preserving overall ship safety via attached conditions.

procedures.action: Comply with any safety requirements attached to an exemption; note exemption automatically ceases if those requirements are not met.

procedures.action: Ensure any exemption, alteration, or cancellation is documented in writing (including electronic form that is legible and retrievable for subsequent reference), specifying effective date and terms.

procedures.action: Secretary of State evaluates whether proposed alternative training arrangements meet the equivalence condition in paragraph (2).

procedures.action: Issue approval, continuation, alteration, or cancellation in writing.

procedures.action: Specify in the written approval the effective date and any terms attached.
procedures.why: Ensures clarity on when and under what conditions the alternative arrangement applies.

procedures.action: Provide reasonable notice before continuing, altering, or cancelling an approval.
procedures.why: Protects parties relying on the approval from abrupt changes.

procedures.action: Transmit written approvals electronically if the output is received in legible form and can be retained for subsequent reference.

constraints: Alternative arrangements must result in safety and pollution-prevention levels at least equivalent to the STCW Convention.

trace.situation: UK Port State Control authority may inspect foreign-flagged (non-UK registered) ships to verify STCW certification and assess watchkeeping standards when there are grounds to believe standards are not being maintained due to specific port incidents.
trace.trigger: An authorised person has grounds to believe watchkeeping standards are not being maintained because, while in a UK port or its approaches, the ship was involved in a collision/grounding/stranding, an unlawful discharge, erratic/unsafe manoeuvring or non-compliance with traffic separation schemes, or was otherwise operated dangerously.

procedures.action: Inspect the non-UK registered ship to verify that seafarers required to be certificated hold valid STCW certificates.
procedures.why: To confirm compliance with certification requirements under STCW Part 4 standards.

procedures.action: Assess the ability of seafarers to maintain required watchkeeping standards where grounds exist based on a qualifying port incident.
procedures.why: A qualifying incident (collision, grounding, unlawful discharge, erratic manoeuvring, dangerous operation) gives reasonable grounds to suspect inadequate watchkeeping.

procedures.action: If a deficiency is found, notify the master of the ship and the ship's flag administration in writing.
procedures.why: Ensures accountability and allows the flag State to take corrective action regarding its vessel.

procedures.action: If the flag administration cannot be informed directly, inform the Consul of the flag State, or in the Consul's absence, the nearest diplomatic representative.
procedures.why: Ensures notification of the flag State is still achieved through diplomatic channels when direct contact is not possible.

constraints: Inspection powers apply only to ships not registered in the United Kingdom.
Assessment of watchkeeping standards requires grounds for believing standards are not maintained, tied to a specific qualifying incident while in a UK port or its approaches.

Deficiencies must be the specific kinds listed (certificate failure, safe manning non-compliance, watch arrangement non-conformity, absence of qualified watch personnel, inability to provide rested crew for watches).
warnings: A finding of deficiency triggers mandatory written notification to both the master and the flag administration.
Inability of the master to provide adequately rested persons for watches is treated as a reportable deficiency.
outcomes: If deficiencies are found, the master and flag administration are formally notified, enabling corrective action.
If the flag administration cannot be reached, diplomatic channels (Consul or nearest diplomatic representative) are used to ensure notification occurs.
key_facts: This inspection authority applies only to non-UK registered ships.
Grounds for watchkeeping assessment include collision, grounding/stranding, unlawful discharge, erratic/unsafe manoeuvring, or otherwise dangerous operation while in a UK port or its approaches.

Five specific deficiency types are defined, including certificate failure, safe manning non-compliance, watch arrangement non-conformity, absence of qualified watch personnel, and inadequate crew rest provision.
Deficiency notifications must be made in writing to the master and the flag administration, or via diplomatic channels if the flag administration cannot be reached directly.

trace.situation: UK STCW regulations set out criminal offences and penalties for training providers, owners, companies, masters, and crew members who contravene specific manning, training, watchkeeping, and documentation requirements.
trace.trigger: A regulated party (training provider, owner, company, master, or crew member) fails to comply with the specific duties listed in regulations 48(13), 51(3), 55, 56, 57, 58, 61, or 62.

procedures.action: Ensure the ship carries a valid safe manning document as required by regulation 55.
procedures.why: Contravention of regulation 55(2)/(3) is an offence for both the company and the master, punishable by fine or imprisonment up to six months.

procedures.action: Maintain proper watchkeeping arrangements at sea and in port, including for ships carrying hazardous cargo.
procedures.why: Regulations 56, 57, and 58 impose watchkeeping duties on the master, breach of which is a punishable offence.

procedures.action: Fulfil master's and crew's responsibilities under regulation 61 and carry all required documents under regulation 62.
procedures.why: Non-compliance by the master or crew with regulation 61(5) or 62 is an offence with penalties including imprisonment.

procedures.action: As owner, ensure hovercraft personnel receive required type rating training per regulation 51(3).

constraints: Offences under regulation 48(13) apply to unapproved training provision or false holding-out as approved.

warnings: Failure to maintain safe manning documentation or watchkeeping arrangements is a criminal offence, not merely an administrative lapse.

outcomes: Non-compliant masters, owners, companies, or crew face summary conviction fines or indictment penalties including imprisonment up to six months.

Regulations 56-58 govern watchkeeping arrangements at sea, in port, and for hazardous cargo ships.

trace.situation: UK Merchant Shipping Regulations establish grounds and procedure for detaining a ship (including non-UK registered ships) for non-compliance with STCW-related requirements.
trace.trigger: A ship fails to correct a deficiency of the kind specified in regulation 64(4) after notification to the master under regulation 64(2), resulting in danger to persons, property or the marine environment; or the ship breaches a term of a granted exemption.

procedures.action: Notify the master of the deficiency pursuant to regulation 64(2).
procedures.why: Gives the master opportunity to correct the deficiency before detention is considered.

procedures.action: Determine whether the deficiency remains uncorrected and poses danger to persons, property or the marine environment, or whether an exemption term has been breached.
procedures.why: These are the specific statutory grounds that make a non-UK registered ship liable to detention.

procedures.action: Serve a detention notice on the master stating the grounds for detention and requiring compliance until release.
procedures.why: Required by the regulation to formally effect and justify the detention.

procedures.action: Apply section 284(1) of the Act to determine who may release the ship and under what conditions.
procedures.why: The detention notice terms must be complied with until released by a person specified under section 284(1).

procedures.action: Allow reference of the detention notice to arbitration under section 96, subject to modifications (certain subsections omitted).
procedures.why: Provides a dispute mechanism while adapting the Act's standard detention arbitration provisions to this regulation.

procedures.action: Immediately inform the ship's flag administration in writing that a non-UK registered ship has been detained.
procedures.why: Statutory obligation on the Secretary of State to notify the flag State of the detention.

procedures.action: If the flag administration cannot be informed directly, notify the Consul of the flag State, or absent a Consul, the nearest diplomatic representative.
procedures.why: Ensures the flag State is reliably informed through alternate diplomatic channels when direct notification is not possible.

constraints: Detention of non-UK registered ships only applies where there is an uncorrected deficiency under regulation 64(4) causing danger, or a breach of exemption terms.
A detention notice must state grounds and require compliance until release by a person under section 284(1) of the Act.
The Secretary of State must inform the flag administration immediately, or diplomatic channels if direct notification is impossible.
Certain subsections of sections 96 and 284(7) of the Act are omitted or modified when applied under this regulation.
warnings: Any ship not complying with these Regulations may be detained in the United Kingdom.
Failure to correct a notified deficiency that causes danger to persons, property, or the marine environment can trigger detention.
Breach of an exemption's terms can also trigger detention.
outcomes: Ship remains detained until released by a person authorized under section 284(1) of the Act.
Flag administration (or its Consul/diplomatic representative) is informed of the detention.
Detention notice terms must be complied with or the ship remains detained.
key_facts: Detention under this regulation applies to both UK-registered and non-UK-registered ships, though specific grounds listed apply to non-UK registered ships.
A detention notice must be served on the master stating the grounds for detention.
The detention notice can be referred to arbitration under a modified version of section 96 of the Act.

trace.situation: Transitional provisions under UK STCW Regulations specifying how certificates, recognitions, and approvals issued under the 2015 Regulations are treated once the new Regulations come into force.
trace.trigger: Coming into force of the new STCW Regulations superseding the 2015 Regulations, requiring continuity of previously issued certificates, recognitions, and approvals.

procedures.action: Treat any certificate of competency, equivalent competency, proficiency, marine engine operator's licence, or type rating training certificate issued under the 2015 Regulations as valid and issued under the new Regulations.
procedures.why: Ensures continuity of seafarer qualifications across the regulatory transition without requiring reissue.

procedures.action: Treat any EEA State or third party State certificate recognition made under 2015 Regulations regulation 32/33 as a recognition under the new Regulations' regulation 36/37.
procedures.why: Preserves validity of prior state-based certificate recognitions.

procedures.action: Treat any party recognised under 2015 Regulations regulation 33A as recognised under new Regulations regulation 38.
procedures.why: Maintains continuity of STCW Convention party recognitions made on or after IP completion day.

procedures.action: Treat any training provider approval or documentary evidence issued under 2015 Regulations regulations 41 or 42 as issued under the corresponding new Regulations (regulations 48, 26(3), 49(2), or 51(4)).
procedures.why: Avoids disruption to approved training providers and previously issued training documentation.

constraints: Certificates remain valid only for the period specified in the original certificate.
Transitional treatment applies only to certificates/recognitions/approvals issued before the new Regulations came into force.
outcomes: Seafarers and training providers retain uninterrupted validity of certificates, recognitions, and approvals despite regulatory transition.
No requirement for re-issuance of existing certificates or approvals solely due to the regulatory change.
key_facts: Certificates covered include certificates of competency, equivalent competency, proficiency, marine engine operator's licences, and high-speed craft/hovercraft type rating training certificates.
Certificate validity periods remain as originally specified, unaffected by the transition.
State and third-party recognitions under the 2015 Regulations carry over to equivalent provisions in the new Regulations.
Training provider approvals and documentary evidence issued under the 2015 Regulations are deemed issued under the corresponding new Regulations provisions.

constraints: First report must be published within five years of the Regulations coming into force.
